key_insight: This paper introduces a real-world, large-scale dataset designed to support automated skill evaluation for central line dressing change procedures. It addresses a major bottleneck in clinical training by enabling more scalable, consistent, and fine-grained assessment than manual observation alone.
problem_solved: Current central line dressing change competency assessment depends heavily on clinical educators manually observing and scoring performance, which is time-consuming, hard to scale, and inconsistent across evaluators. The paper tackles the lack of a robust dataset needed to train and validate AI systems for automated evaluation.
method: Collected a real-world, large-scale dataset from central line dressing change procedures.
Designed the dataset to support automated assessment of procedural skill and competency evaluation.
Targeted a healthcare training setting where reliable, granular, and scalable evaluation is needed.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this dataset creates a foundation for developing computer vision and sequence modeling systems for clinical skill assessment. It can accelerate research on automated evaluation tools that reduce educator workload and improve consistency in healthcare training.

paper_title: The Collection of a Real-World, Large-Scale Dataset for Automated Skill Evaluation in Central Line Dressing Change
paper_authors: Ummey Tanin, Shannan K. Hamlin, Hsin-Mei Chen,  Peizhu,  Qian
